context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Replace the dynamic copy with an explicit allow-list. Define a constant set of fields that may be returned to each requester role (for example, PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS = ['id', 'name', 'avatarUrl'], and a larger set only for the record owner or an authorised admin). Do not trust requestedFields as given. Intersect it with the allow-list for the caller's role, and ignore any unknown or disallowed names: `const allowed = ALLOWED_FIELDS_FOR(requester); for (const field of requestedFields) { if (allowed.includes(field) && user?.data[field] !== undefined) baseUser[field] = user.data[field]; }`. Build the response from these explicit field lists rather than spreading or serialising the whole user.data object or nested records, so sensitive values such as password hashes, tokens, internal flags, and other personal data are never copied. Put the allow-list and filtering in one shared serializer, and use it on every route that returns user records, so the same field limits apply everywhere, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires. Add tests that request disallowed and nested fields and confirm they are omitted for each role.
